headline: Approved changes to CTE admissions and middle school pathway policies, and a five-year lease for ten special education buses.
summary: Dr. Marco Andrade and Dr. Andrew Lampi presented 2026 test results, graduation rates, and dropout rates. A student petition about bathroom conditions at Sullivan Middle School was held. A request for a 50/50 arts magnet school at Burncoat came up during the boundary realignment discussion.
decisions: Held public petition c&p 6-14 on bathroom conditions at Sullivan Middle School, 8-0.
Approved the consent agenda as submitted, 8-0.
Approved and filed the superintendent's report on student assessment and performance data, 8-0.
Approved the Operations and Governance report on the boundary realignment project, 8-0, and held the item for future forums.
Approved proposed changes to the CTE admissions policy, with Member Johnson's amendment, and the middle school pathway exploration policy for 2026-2027, 8-0.
Held gb 4-114 on teacher sick time reports for future updates, 7-0.
Approved and filed the update on the City IT Department moving out of Worcester Technical High School, 7-0.
Approved a five-year lease for ten special education buses, 6-0.

 Public Petition Backup for c&p 6-14

K. Report of the Superintendent  
 ros 6-14 (Administration) 
   (October 22, 2026) 
Student Assessment and Performance Data 
 
Dr. Marco Andrade and Dr. Andrew Lampi presented the WPS accountability data and 
test results. Overall, the 2026 District percentage of targets met is currently 46%, 
compared with  47% in 2024 and 2025, and 45% in 2026. From 2024 to 2025, 6 
schools increased their progress toward target level. From 2025 to 2026, 14 schools 
increased their progress toward target level. 
 
Columbus park, Elm Park, Flagg Street and McGrath Elementary met or exceeded 
targets by 75% or more. Drs. Andrade and Lampi presented detailed data on 
achievements in ELA, math, and science and compared that data with other state 
numbers and comparisons with comparable urban districts in Massachusetts.  
 
Growth indicators data in ELA and math were presented also. The data included 
grades 3-8 and grade 10 over the course of the 2024, 2025, and 2026 school years. 
 
English language proficiency target indicators were then presented. WPS exceeded 
targets for the Non-High School level earning the maximum 4 accountability points. 
WPS has met or exceeded the annual target for three consecutive years. Chronic 
absenteeism was discussed. Overall, chronic absenteeism percentages remained 
relatively the same since 2025. 
 
Drs. Andrade and Lampi provided the data on the 4-year graduation rate. WPS tends 
to be closer to the state’s average than that of our urban counterparts. The 4-year 
graduation rate is relatively unchanged in 2026 (graduating class of 2025). High 
schools across the state had nearly a one point improvement in graduation rates while 
comparable urban districts increased nearly four points, closing the gap with WPS. 
  
The annual dropout rate is relatively unchanged in 2026 (graduating class of 2025) 
but remains low at 2%.The annual dropout rate improved slightly at the state level 
and more so for other urban districts. MCAS achievement for groups of students, 
including English language learners (present and past), students with disabilities, and 
Hispanic and Latino/Hispanic students was presented as well.  
 
Highlights of the report include WPS has made steady incremental gains at the district 
level across both 2025 and 2026. There were only three declines in performance in 
2026 which were for high school achievement (ELA, Math, Science) and which 
matches the statewide pattern of decline since MCAS was removed as a graduation 
requirement. WPS had more schools increase their overall annual progress toward 
target levels in 2026 (14) than 2025 (6).  
 
Next steps include: strengthening district support systems for schools around high 
quality teaching and learning, strengthening teacher Professional Learning

Communities (PLCs) to consistently review student work and performance and the use 
of Walkthrough data to provide feedback and align on instructional practices, adoption 
and implementation of new high-quality instructional materials (HQIM) particularly at 
the secondary level for English Learners to better support their language acquisition,  
improved oversight, procedures and systems for Attendance Matters effort, and new 
curriculum and training plan for Special Education Autism programs. 
 
Superintendent Allen stated that WPS is on the right track with high quality 
instruction, educators and curriculum. 
 
Member Biancheria expressed concern with some of the data in advanced coursework 
with WPS being well below the state average. Dr. Emily Lehman, Director of College 
and Career Readiness, expressed confidence that WPS is going in the right direction to 
increase the number of students engaged in advanced coursework. 
 
Member Biancheria made a motion to receive raw numbers for chronic 
absenteeism in grades K-12.  
 
Member Binienda asked what the administration attributes to the increase of the 
extended engagement rate. Dr. Andrade could not say the reason why, just that this is 
what the data indicated. She also asked who the other urban districts are and what 
were possible reasons for other urban districts being so far ahead of Worcester in 
advanced coursework.  
 
Member Johnson made a motion to receive information regarding 
accountability scores from all schools to highlight which schools need more 
attention. 
 
Member Alvarez commented on several points in the presentation. First, she was 
pleased to see that chronic absenteeism is on the decline but asked what evidence  
there is that current WPS strategies in place are working. She also asked how WPS 
uses the absentee data to understand our students and put in place measurable 
strategies, goals, and a regular reporting schedule. 
  
Madeline Trombley, Student Representative from South High, asked Mr. Andrade to 
clarify data around advanced coursework to which Dr. Andrade answered to her 
satisfaction.  
 
A motion was made to approve and file this item. On a voice vote of 8-0, the 
motion passed unanimously. Mayor Petty was absent for the vote.

Boundary Realignment Presentation 
To consider the recommendations of the district boundary and realignment

Results: The report was approved and the item was held for future forums. 
 
Member Mailman spoke regarding her concerns for and desire for more dual 
language schools and magnet schools in the North quadrant. Superintendent 
Allen, along with Nick Stellitano and Katie Tartalglia from Dillinger Associates 
addressed her concerns, reminding everyone that there are only so many 
buildings but equity in programming is a top priority in this project.  
 
Member Mailman also asked how transportation plans will be presented to the 
Committee, especially if two new schools will be added. Superintendent Allen 
explained the administration’s plans. She also asked  about sub-separate 
classrooms. Katie Tartaglia explained how the elementary schools will be set up 
and there should be no changes to their locations at this point.  
 
Member Mailman made a motion to receive cost data regarding the 
boundary realignment project.  
 
She mentioned she would like to have a 50/50 arts magnet school at Burncoat. 
She stated that our students and families deserve this and it can be used as a 
tool to recruit students and educators.  
 
A motion was made to approve the report of O & G. On a voice vote of 
8-0, the motion passed unanimously. Mayor Petty was absent for the 
vote.

Technical High School admissions section on siblings admission status
